title: Keep a live worker's completion bytes out of the next seat's recovery checkpoint
description:
DEFECT, observed twice on 2026-09-11, both with evidence in git.

When a worker calls complete_task, the task flips to REVIEW immediately, but the worker's CLI keeps running for a while and its wrapper post-flight (which makes the feat/fix completion commit) only runs when the session exits. A QA seat can claim the REVIEW task inside that window. The QA wrapper's pre-flight then finds the task's per-task baseline (<gitdir>/moe/baseline/<taskId>.tsv, kept until DONE and shared by every seat in the checkout) plus dirty paths, treats them as a crashed session's leftovers, and lands them as a recovery checkpoint. The worker was not crashed. It was about to commit those bytes itself. When it exits, its completion commit finds almost nothing left.

EVIDENCE
task-a135d4d6 (assertAttemptCurrent guard):
- REVIEW at 10:27:44, qa-8db40c97 claimed at 10:28:12.
- ac6c9dc  wip(task-a135d4d6) [status=REVIEW role=qa cli-exit=0] recovered, landed 10:28:16. Contains the ENTIRE implementation: util/enforcement.ts +144, util/enforcement.test.ts +472, plus two board JSONs.
- 7cdcf2e  feat(task-a135d4d6), the worker's completion commit, landed 10:29:55. Contains ONLY .moe/tasks/task-a135d4d6....json.
task-435683c2 (JetBrains time-cap parser removal): same shape. 5a7d27a is a role=qa recovered wip at REVIEW, and e0ed8ca feat contains only its own board JSON.

WHY IT MATTERS (no bytes are lost, everything is on the branch and pushed)
1. CLAUDE.md tells QA to audit with git show on the completion commit. For these tasks that shows zero code. A careful reviewer either rejects work that is fine or approves without having seen the diff.
2. qa_approve's NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT gate does NOT fire, because a completion commit exists after reviewStartedAt. It is just empty. The soft gate is satisfied by a commit that proves nothing.
3. History lies. The feat commit for a feature contains no feature, and the code is attributed to role=qa under a wip subject. scripts/analyze-task-metrics.mjs --commits buckets it as wip.

It is systematic, not a one-off: it fires whenever QA claims faster than the worker's CLI exits. Both REVIEW handoffs today hit it.

NOT PRESCRIBING THE FIX. Directions the architect should weigh, each with a real cost:
(a) Recovery runs only when the task's previous holder is gone (missing from the worker map or DEAD), not whenever a baseline and dirty paths exist. Needs a liveness signal the wrapper can read.
(b) The worker lands its completion commit BEFORE complete_task makes the task visible to QA. Cleanest invariant, biggest behavior change.
(c) The pre-flight recovery skips a task that entered REVIEW within a short grace window. Simplest to write, and a timing heuristic that will be wrong under load.
Whatever is chosen, a genuine crash must still be recovered exactly as today. The recovery path exists because of the 2026-08-28 lost-code incident, and weakening it is worse than this defect.
definitionOfDone: Reproduced first: a regression case in the launcher postflight harness (scripts/tests/postflight.sh and its .ps1 sibling) in which a second seat's pre-flight runs against a task whose worker has reached REVIEW but not yet exited, and which fails on the current code by showing the implementation paths landing in the second seat's recovery checkpoint.
After the fix, in that race the worker's completion commit contains the task's implementation paths, and the second seat's pre-flight lands no recovery checkpoint for them.

A genuine crash is still recovered unchanged: a case where the previous holder is gone (missing or DEAD) still lands its dirty bytes as a recovery checkpoint on the next pre-flight, and that existing behavior's tests still pass.
The fix is implemented identically in scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-agent.sh, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.
Both postflight harnesses pass, run sequentially with MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180, and the command and result are recorded in the completion verification.
docs/roles/qa.md or the moe-qa-loop skill states how to audit a task whose code spans several commits, if the chosen fix does not make the completion commit self-contained in every case.
taskRails: Both launchers or neither: moe-agent.ps1 and moe-agent.sh must change together.
Never weaken crash recovery to fix this; a lost-byte regression is strictly worse than a misattributed commit.
Pathspec-only staging stays: no git add -A or -u, and no bare git commit against the shared index.
Planning and design review first: this is the landing path, so the plan goes to the human before a worker implements it.

implementationPlan.description: RED FIRST, IN BOTH HARNESSES. Add the reproduction to scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, leaving existing cases untouched. The case: a task has a per-task baseline and dirty implementation paths, and its previous holder is STILL RUNNING - spawn a real long-sleeping child process so there is a genuine live process id to probe, rather than faking one. Run a second seat's pre-flight recovery against that state and assert that today it lands those paths as a recovery checkpoint, which is the defect. Then assert what must be true after the fix: no recovery checkpoint, the dirty paths still present and unstaged, and a named skip line naming the task. Add the crash case in the same shape and assert it BOTH before and after the fix, because it is the behaviour that must not move: a marker whose process is gone still recovers exactly as today. Add the back-compatibility case: no marker file at all, which is every task in flight when this change lands, still recovers as today. Run both harnesses sequentially on a quiet box with MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 and save the red output. Never pipe a harness through grep with pipefail set, which turns a real failure into a silent exit code.

RED FIRST, IN BOTH HARNESSES. Scenario M2 added to scripts/tests/postflight.sh (after scenario M, 1369-1590) and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 (after scenario M, 1093-1290). No existing case touched; the two scenario counters go 25 -> 26.

FIVE SUB-CASES (identical in both twins, same names, same skip-line literal):
(a) THE MEASURED RACE, real claim shape: task record at REVIEW, FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=resume, role=qa, worker id qa-scope-m2 -- a QA seat claiming a REVIEW task whose worker is still running. Asserts, after the fix: NO `MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED task=task-resume`; the EXACT skip line `MOE_CHECKPOINT_SKIPPED_LIVE_OWNER task=task-resume pid=<livepid> host=<host> worker=worker-owner reason=live`; that skip line appears BEFORE the CLI launch (same ordering pin scenario M uses); NO commit for the task whose subject ends in ` recovered`; and the marker file still names the live owner's pid (a seat that stands down must not stamp its own id over it, or the NEXT seat sees a dead owner and steals).
(b) SAME GUARD ON THE IDLE (BLOCKED-hold) PATH, where the pre-flight is the ONLY git actor -- so the plan's three required post-fix facts are observed DIRECTLY rather than inferred: zero commits for the task, `git status --porcelain` still showing `?? impl.txt` (present AND unstaged), the baseline .tsv still on disk and still ` landed=0`. Also re-asserts the BLOCKED suppression line so the sub-case cannot silently stop exercising that path.
(c) CRASH -- MUST NOT MOVE. Spawns a real child, reads its start token, kills it and REAPS it (`wait` / `WaitForExit` + a re-probe that throws if it is somehow alive), so the id is definitively dead and not merely unlikely. Asserts MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED still fires, the checkpoint carries EXACTLY `.moe/tasks/<id>.json impl.txt`, and the stale marker is deleted.
(d) PROCESS-ID REUSE. Live pid, deliberately corrupted start token (`$start` + "999"): must recover, else a long-lived box would suppress crash recovery by coincidence. The sh twin skips this LOUDLY with a printed line when the platform exposes no start token (identity-only probe by design); the ps1 twin hard-fails if it cannot read one, since Get-Process always can on Windows.
(e) BACK-COMPATIBILITY: baseline, no marker at all -- every task in flight when this lands. Must recover exactly as today. (Scenario M is itself a second, untouched instance of this shape and stays green.)

REAL PROCESSES, NOT FAKES, per the plan: bash spawns `sleep 600 &`; ps1 spawns `Start-Process $psExe -Command 'Start-Sleep -Seconds 600' -WindowStyle Hidden`. Both register the pid in a new harness-level list killed from the existing EXIT trap / outer finally (`LIVE_PIDS` in .sh, `$script:M2LivePids` in .ps1) so a failing case cannot leak a ten-minute sleep.

ANTI-FALSE-GREEN: no producer is ever piped into `grep -q` under `set -o pipefail` (the 141 trap in mem:gotcha-bash-cmd-d-c-false-green) -- `m2_subjects()` and the status check write to a FILE first and grep the file. The skip assertion is the WHOLE line including pid, host, worker and `reason=live`, so the live-probe branch cannot be satisfied by the conservative foreign-host fallback.

    [info] MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT: task task-resume -- no changed candidate paths (already landed, ...)
    SCENARIO M2 FAILED: (a) the second seat recovered a LIVE owner's baseline

    [info] MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT: task task-resume -- no attributable changes to commit ...
    MOE_POSTFLIGHT_FAILURE_LINE=1176

That is the production evidence shape reproduced exactly: the second seat's pre-flight lands everything, and the owner's own landing then reports NOTHING-TO-COMMIT -- ac6c9dc/7cdcf2e and b5925e2 in miniature. Every case before M2 stayed green in both runs; the failure is the first M2 assertion, not an earlier regression.

Syntax gates: `bash -n scripts/tests/postflight.sh` clean; `[Parser]::ParseFile` on postflight.ps1 reports no errors. CRLF+BOM preserved on the .ps1 (`file` still reports "UTF-8 (with BOM) text, with CRLF line terminators").

implementationPlan.description: WRITE AND REMOVE THE LIVE-SESSION MARKER, BOTH WRAPPERS IN LOCKSTEP. Edit scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-agent.sh together - same behaviour, same operator strings, same code names - because a one-sided change fails parity-check and leaves half the fleet broken. Add a marker beside the existing baseline, at the sibling path under the git directory that the baseline helper already computes, named by task id. Contents: the wrapper's own process id, the host name, the worker id, the session id and the process start time. The start time is what makes the later probe safe against process-id reuse, which is a real hazard on a long-lived box. Write it in the SAME pre-flight block that takes the baseline, so a session either has both or neither, and write it on the resume path too - a resumed session is just as live as a fresh one. Remove it wherever the session's ownership ends: the normal post-flight beside the baseline prune, and every abnormal exit path - in bash both the EXIT trap and the interrupt handler, in PowerShell the equivalent finally and interrupt handling - because a Ctrl+C that leaves a marker behind would suppress a legitimate recovery until a human cleared it. Error handling: a marker that cannot be written is a warning, not a failure, and the session proceeds - the marker is a safety improvement, and refusing to run without it would be a worse outcome than the defect it prevents. Keep pathspec-only staging untouched; this step adds no git operations at all.
implementationPlan.note:
WRITE AND REMOVE THE LIVE-SESSION MARKER, BOTH WRAPPERS IN LOCKSTEP. No git operations added; staging untouched.

FORMAT (identical byte-for-byte in both wrappers, one LF-terminated line at <gitdir>/moe/baseline/<taskId>.live, the sibling of the baseline the existing helper already computes):
  #moe-live v1 task=<id> pid=<n> host=<h> ns=<n> worker=<id> session=<sid> start=<tok>

The plan named pid/host/worker/session/start. I added `ns` (the pid NAMESPACE: win32 | msys | posix) because step 1 measured that a Git Bash pid and a Windows pid are different namespaces on the SAME machine with the SAME host name ($(hostname)=Yaron-PC vs $env:COMPUTERNAME=YARON-PC), and WSL2 defaults its hostname to the Windows machine name -- precisely the cross-mount case the plan calls out. Host name alone does not discriminate an unprobeable marker; without `ns` a ps1 seat would probe an MSYS id against the Windows process table and could read a LIVE owner as dead, which is the byte-loss direction the task rail forbids. `ns` mismatch routes to the same conservative skip as a host mismatch.

BASH (scripts/moe-agent.sh), new section between baseline_mark_landed and commit_scope (2231-2381):
  live_marker_path / live_marker_ns / live_marker_host / proc_start_token / live_marker_write / live_marker_remove / proc_alive / live_marker_state / live_marker_foreign_live.
PS1 (scripts/moe-agent.ps1), new section between Set-MoeBaselineLanded and Get-MoeTaskDeclaredSets (1886-2027):
  Get-MoeLiveMarkerPath / Get-MoeLiveMarkerHost / Get-MoeLiveMarkerNs / Get-MoeProcStartToken / Write-MoeLiveMarker / Remove-MoeLiveMarker / Get-MoeLiveMarkerFirstLine / Get-MoeLiveMarkerState / Test-MoeLiveMarkerForeignLive.
The ps1 path helper carries the SAME '^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$' id whitelist as Get-MoeBaselinePath, since the id reaches a path join. Both write .tmp + rename; both write LF, so each wrapper reads the other's marker.

START TOKEN. bash: /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 (starttime in clock ticks), counted after the LAST ')' because comm can contain spaces and parentheses -- verified present on Git Bash/MSYS (measured), and the same file exists on Linux and WSL. MSYS `ps` has no `-o` flag, so there is deliberately NO second source: an empty token degrades the probe to identity alone, stated in the function comment as the plan asked. ps1: (Get-Process -Id n).StartTime.ToUniversalTime().Ticks.

WRITE SITES -- exactly where the baseline is taken, so a session has both or neither:
  sh preflight_landing step 4, immediately after the successful baseline_write (4251-4259);
  ps1 Invoke-MoePreflightBaseline, immediately after Write-MoeBaseline (3555-3565).
That block is on the launch path AND the resume path (a resumed session is as live as a fresh one), which the plan required.

ONE ADDITION BEYOND THE PLAN'S LETTER, and it is load-bearing: the write does NOT overwrite a marker already held by a LIVE foreign owner (live_marker_foreign_live / Test-MoeLiveMarkerForeignLive; it logs "[attribution] leaving the live-session marker of <id> to its current owner (<worker> pid=<n>)"). Without it the guard is self-defeating: seat B stands down for live seat A, then stamps its OWN id over the marker; A's post-flight then removes a marker naming B, and a third seat sees no owner and steals B's live bytes -- the same defect one hop later. Scenario M2-a asserts the marker still names the original owner's pid after the run, so this is pinned by test, not by comment.

REMOVAL SITES -- every exit that ends this session's ownership:
  sh: cleanup_temp (the EXIT trap, 122-132), guarded by `type -t` like its neighbours. Step 1 verified the INT/TERM trap ends in `exit 0`, which FIRES the EXIT trap, so this single site is the union of Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and a set -e abort -- a second removal in the interrupt handler would be dead code. Plus the post-flight, at the end of the whole landing block beside MOE_LANDING_DONE=true (6329-6333), which covers every LANDING_MODE including `none`.
  ps1: the outer `finally` (5342-5350) -- the file's own measured comment at 363-375 says the CancelKeyPress and PowerShell.Exiting handlers are INERT on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and that this finally is what actually runs on Ctrl+C, so it is the equivalent site. Plus the post-flight beside $moeLandingDone = $true (5297-5301).
Removal is OURS ONLY: a byte-identical match against the line this session wrote ($script:MoeLiveMarkerLine / $MOE_LIVE_MARKER_LINE). Deleting a peer's marker would re-arm the theft. On a rescue/refusal the baseline is deliberately KEPT and the marker IS removed -- that is what lets the next pre-flight recover it.

ERROR HANDLING, as the plan required: a marker that cannot be written prints "[WARN] [attribution] could not write the live-session marker for <id> -- a peer's pre-flight may recover this session's work as a checkpoint." and the session PROCEEDS. Refusing to run without a marker would be worse than the defect it prevents.

VERIFICATION (this step; the wired gate is step 4

implementationPlan.description: GATE THE RECOVERY ON A REAL PROCESS PROBE, BOTH WRAPPERS IN LOCKSTEP. In the pre-flight recovery block of each wrapper - the one that currently lands a checkpoint and prints MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED whenever a baseline and dirty paths exist - consult the marker before doing anything. Four outcomes, and each one matters. No marker: recover exactly as today, which keeps every task already in flight working when this lands. Marker whose process id is this process: it is our own session, so proceed as today. Marker whose process is ALIVE and is not ours, with a matching recorded start time: SKIP the recovery, leave the baseline and the dirty paths exactly as they are so the real owner can still land them, and print a named line in the existing MOE_CHECKPOINT_ family so scripts/tests/parity-check.sh enforces it across both wrappers automatically. Marker whose process is GONE, or whose start time does not match the live process of that id: the owner crashed or the id was reused, so delete the stale marker and recover exactly as today - this is the 2026-08-28 lost-code path and a task rail forbids weakening it. Probe locally: Get-Process in PowerShell, kill -0 in bash, with the start time read where it is cheap and the probe degrading to identity alone when it is not, saying so in a comment. One case needs an explicit decision rather than a guess: a marker written by a DIFFERENT host, which happens in this repository whenever a Windows seat and a WSL seat share the checkout through a mount and cannot see each other's process ids - the bash pre-flight already faces exactly this with a Windows-owned daemon record and solves it by probing another channel. Here, skip the recovery and warn with the same named code plus the recorded host, because refusing to steal is the safe direction and a human can clear a marker; do not silently recover across a boundary you cannot probe.
implementationPlan.note:
GATE THE RECOVERY ON A REAL PROCESS PROBE, BOTH WRAPPERS IN LOCKSTEP. Scenario M2 is now GREEN in both harnesses; every pre-existing case stayed green.

THE GATE. sh preflight_landing step 3 (4186-4215); ps1 Invoke-MoeRecoveryCheck (3502-3531). The marker is consulted BEFORE anything is touched, and the landing call is now additionally conditioned on the state. Four outcomes, all four wired:
  none | self -> recover exactly as before. `none` is every task already in flight when this lands (back-compat, pinned by M2-e and by the untouched scenario M). `self` is the idle/resume paths re-entering the pre-flight for a task this very process already holds.
  live        -> SKIP. Baseline and dirty paths left exactly as they are so the real owner lands them itself.
  foreign     -> SKIP, the host/namespace we cannot probe. Names the recorded host and tells the operator which file to delete by hand if that session is known gone.
  stale       -> delete the stale marker, then recover exactly as before. Process gone OR start token mismatched (recycled id). This is the 2026-08-28 lost-code path; it does not move.

NAMED CODE: MOE_CHECKPOINT_SKIPPED_LIVE_OWNER, emitted identically by both wrappers as
  MOE_CHECKPOINT_SKIPPED_LIVE_OWNER task=<id> pid=<n> host=<h> worker=<id> reason=live|foreign-host
It is in the MOE_CHECKPOINT_ family, which parity-check.sh extracts from both wrappers and diffs, so cross-wrapper symmetry is enforced with no harness edit -- as planned. MUTATION-PROVED rather than assumed: renaming the literal in moe-agent.ps1 only makes parity-check fail loudly ("MOE_CHECKPOINT_* codes only in moe-agent.sh: MOE_CHECKPOINT_SKIPPED_LIVE_OWNER"), exit 1; restored byte-exact and it passes again, with no residue and the BOM/CRLF intact.

PROBE. bash proc_alive: /proc is authoritative where it exists (Linux, WSL and MSYS/Git Bash all have it, measured), so an absent /proc/<pid> is a definitive "gone" and the crash path is unchanged; `kill -0` is the fallback elsewhere, with its EPERM caveat written down. ps1: Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue, $null meaning gone. A probe that FAILS TO ANSWER (a throw, or an unreadable StartTime) is treated as ALIVE in both wrappers, with the reason stated inline -- refusing to steal is recoverable by a human, a wrong recovery is the byte-loss class this exists to prevent.

ONE REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED MID-STEP, worth recording. The first green run showed the gate firing correctly but printing `pid= host= worker=` -- empty. Cause: bash `live_marker_state` originally ECHOED its state, so callers wrapped it in `$( ... )`, and that subshell discarded every MOE_LIVE_OWNER_* assignment made inside it. Reworked to ASSIGN MOE_LIVE_STATE instead of echoing, with a comment saying exactly why so nobody "tidies" it back into a `$(...)` call. The ps1 twin returns a value and sets $script:MoeLiveOwner, which has no such hazard; the mechanisms differ, the behaviour and every operator string do not. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The operator reviewed the three options the filer listed and chose this one, which the task rails required before any implementation. Option (b), landing the completion commit before the task becomes visible to QA, is the cleanest invariant and was NOT rejected on merit - it is simply already scoped in Wave 1 as the finalizing phase plus the finalize tool, and a Wave 0 epic rail forbids widening into Wave 1 work. When that lands it supersedes this guard, which is fine: this one is cheap and removable. Option (c), a timing grace window, was ruled out by the filer on evidence and is ruled out again here - a worker's tail after completing a task is unbounded, so any window is a guess. The filer's option (a) as literally written, keyed on the board's view of the holder, was rejected on inspection: a hard-crashed worker is not marked dead, so that predicate would stop recovering exactly the crash it exists for. Keying on a real local process probe keeps the spirit of (a) while preserving crash recovery. Faking the probe in tests was rejected in favour of spawning a genuine sleeping process, because a fake would not catch a wrong probe invocation.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Verified live on 2026-09-11. The recovery path fires on the wrong predicate: it asks whether a baseline and dirty paths exist, which is true both when a session crashed and when a session is still running and about to commit. Nothing in it asks whether anyone still owns those bytes. The task rails and the project's own history close off the obvious liveness signals - a hard-crashed worker is NOT marked dead on the board because there is no graceful deregistration, and idle time is explicitly not evidence of death, since the project deliberately removed idle-based auto-release for in-flight work. So board liveness cannot discriminate. What CAN is a local fact the wrapper owns end to end: whether the process that wrote the marker is still running in this checkout. Per-task baselines already live under the git directory and are already shared by every seat in the checkout, so a sibling marker inherits exactly the right scope with no new concept. The cross-host case is not hypothetical here: a Windows seat and a WSL seat share this checkout through a mount and cannot probe each other's process ids, and the bash pre-flight already meets that exact problem with a Windows-owned daemon record and solves it by probing a different channel rather than guessing - the same conservatism applies. parity-check already extracts the MOE_CHECKPOINT_ family from both wrappers, so naming the skip code inside it enforces cross-wrapper symmetry with no harness edit.
planningNotes.risks: The overriding constraint is a task rail: never weaken crash recovery. Every branch of the new guard must be walked explicitly against that, and the probe failing or throwing must be treated as ALIVE - refusing to steal is recoverable by a human, whereas a wrong recovery is the byte-loss class this whole mechanism exists to prevent. Process-id reuse is real on a long-lived box, which is why the marker records a start time and the probe compares it. Both wrappers must change together or parity-check fails. The marker must be removed on the abnormal exit paths as well as the normal one - bash has two traps and PowerShell its own equivalents - or a Ctrl+C suppresses legitimate recovery until a human clears the file. A missing marker must keep recovering, or every task in flight at the moment this lands would stop being recoverable. Leave the baseline in place on a skip, or the real owner loses its attribution. Do not touch staging: pathspec-only, no whole-tree operation. The documentation note goes in the reference file, not the role doc, which the linter caps at 40 lines. Run the two postflight harnesses sequentially on a quiet box with MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 and never pipe them through grep with pipefail set. This task is epic-final, so its landing runs the full quality gate.
